claim_tested: AIG1 and ADTRP are membrane hydrolases with Thr/His catalysis
key_finding: Activity-based protein profiling identifies AIG1 and ADTRP as multipass transmembrane Thr hydrolases that degrade FAHFAs; cell-active covalent inhibitors block FAHFA hydrolysis
context: Human/mouse cell lysates and intact cells; recombinant expression
confidence_and_limitations: High for enzymology. The abstract makes no subcellular compartment claim beyond multipass transmembrane. This is the sole ECO:0000269 reference behind UniProt's 'Cell membrane' term for AIG1.

claim_tested: ADTRP resides at the plasma membrane
key_finding: ADTRP colocalises with TFPI and caveolin-1 in endothelial cells; Triton X-114 extraction places ADTRP in lipid rafts/caveolae
context: Cultured human endothelial cells; overexpression and shRNA
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Overexpression plus antibody colocalisation; caveolar fractions can carry ER contaminants. Concerns ADTRP only; no AIG1 data. Supports a PM pool for ADTRP.

claim_tested: KxKxx is a bona fide coatomer-binding retrieval motif distinct from KKxx
key_finding: Crystal structures of alpha-COP and beta'-COP bound to KKxx, KxKxx, RKxx and KxHxx; KKxx and KxKxx bind with lysines transposed across two acidic patches; C-terminal carboxylate enforces positional context
confidence_and_limitations: High. Establishes that a Lys at -3 plus Lys at -5 with a free C-terminal carboxylate is a recognised signal

claim_tested: A KxKxx terminus is sufficient to hold a membrane protein in the ER
key_finding: Converting the SARS-CoV-2 spike KxHxx to KxKxx retains spike in the ER and prevents glycan processing, cleavage and transport to the plasma membrane
confidence_and_limitations: High for motif sufficiency. Different protein and topology (type I tail) from AIG1's polytopic tail.

claim_tested: Dilysine ER retention motifs act through coatomer
key_finding: Yeast and mammalian ER retention motifs bind coatomer in cell lysates; mutations that abolish retention also abolish coatomer binding
confidence_and_limitations: High for mechanism; historical study with KKxx motifs on type I proteins.

claim_tested: AIG1 has 6 TM helices with both termini cytosolic
key_finding: Helix-bundle alignment |cos|=0.92; res1 z=-19.7 A and res238 z=-43.5 A on the same side of the bilayer; mean pLDDT 93.8
context: AlphaFold DB v6 model of human AIG1
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high. Prediction
column8: not experiment. Termini have low pLDDT (36 and 56) so their exact position is uncertain
column9: but sidedness follows from the even helix count.

claim_tested: Catalytic Thr43 and His134 face the lumen or the cytosol
key_finding: Both sit inside the bilayer (z=+5.7 A and +4.6 A from mid-plane, pLDDT 97-98) with Thr43:OG1 to His134:NE2 = 3.08 A; neither faces an aqueous compartment
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high. The seed hypothesis's framing of 'which side the catalytic residues face' does not apply; the active site is intramembrane.

citation: This work (UniProt vertebrate orthologs; n=186 AIG1 species)
claim_tested: AIG1's C-terminal KxKxx is under selection
key_finding: Lys at -3 in 82.3% (binomial p=1.4e-137 vs 7.5% tail background), Lys at -5 in 74.7% (p=1.9e-114), Lys at -4 in only 3.2%; flanking residues vary while the K-x-K-x-x register is retained
context: UniProt taxid 7742, anchored on W[LIVM]NH[GASC]MHT, one entry per species
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high. Ortholog set includes automatic gene models; species scored as lacking the motif are enriched for truncated predictions (chimp

citation: This work (UniProt vertebrate orthologs; n=352 ADTRP species)
claim_tested: ADTRP shares AIG1's ER-retrieval motif
key_finding: Dilysine in only 19.6% of species; Lys at -5 in 8.2% (p=0.30, not above background); commonest vertebrate C-termini are WGQSKFCF/IWGQSKFS/WGQSKFSS with no dilysine; the human RKKRK form is primate-restricted and mouse and rat lack it
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Divergence after a shared Trp-Gly suggests an alternative terminal exon that the ortholog filter cannot resolve without transcript evidence.

claim_tested: A C-terminal dilysine predicts ER membrane localisation
key_finding: Among 5230 human TM proteins the motif is 8.6-fold enriched at the ER membrane (11.30% vs 1.46%, Fisher p=7.5e-39), flat at the Golgi (OR 0.82, p=0.59) and depleted at the plasma membrane (OR 0.25, p=4.9e-17); but of 63 dilysine-ending proteins with >=6 TM, 49.2% are annotated ER membrane and 41.3% plasma membrane
context: UniProt reviewed human proteome with GO CC annotations
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. GO annotations are themselves partly inferred and multi-compartment proteins are counted in both columns
column8: so the positive predictive value is an estimate. Shows the motif is informative but not decisive alone.

claim_tested: AIG1's architecture matches ER enzymes rather than PM proteins
key_finding: 44 multipass ER-membrane proteins carry a C-terminal dilysine, including ELOVL1/2/3/4/7, HACD2/3/4, CERS1, LPCAT3, MBOAT1/4, EBP, EBPL, HMGCR, TM6SF2, HHATL (KQDKEKPE, nearly identical to AIG1's EKEKPKLE), TMEM41B, LCLAT1, ZDHHC4/6
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Guilt by architecture
column8: not direct evidence. The plasma-membrane counter-set is dominated by olfactory and taste receptors (15 of 32 multipass cases) where the motif is plausibly incidental.

claim_tested: AIG1 is at the plasma membrane or the ER
key_finding: IF assigns AIG1 to Mitochondria (main) and Cytosol (additional); reliability 'Supported'
confidence_and_limitations: Low. Neither compartment is compatible with a 6-TM protein. Treat as uninformative or artefactual rather than as evidence against ER.

claim_tested: ADTRP is at the plasma membrane
key_finding: IF assigns ADTRP to Nucleoli; reliability 'Uncertain'
confidence_and_limitations: Low. Self-declared uncertain; incompatible with a 6-TM protein.

claim_tested: Existing annotation justifies 'cell membrane' for AIG1
key_finding: SUBCELLULAR LOCATION 'Cell membrane; Multi-pass membrane protein' rests on a single ECO:0000269 citation (PMID:27018888); TM helices are ECO:0000255 prediction and topological domains are ECO:0000305 curator inference
confidence_and_limitations: High for what the record says. The compartment assignment is not backed by an AIG1 localisation experiment.

claim_tested: Consensus TM predictors independently confirm 6 TM helices in AIG1
key_finding: An independent Kyte-Doolittle + Eisenberg + White-Wimley consensus (19-aa window, z-scored) never calls 6 segments at any threshold from z>+0.90 to z>-0.20 (AIG1: 0,2,3,4,5,5,5,5,5; ADTRP: 1,2,2,3,4,5,5,5,5). AIG1's helices are 38.5% polar/aromatic (TM1 55.6%, TM5 47.8%, TM4 45.0%)
context: Human AIG1 and ADTRP sequences, UniProt TM boundaries as ground truth
confidence_and_limitations: High for the negative result. DeepTMHMM/Phobius/TOPCONS were NOT run (no reachable endpoint). The 6-helix model therefore rests on AlphaFold plus UniProt ECO:0000255, which are not methodologically independent. The polar composition is expected for an intramembrane Thr43/His134 active site.

claim_tested: TM hydrophobicity and length discriminate ER from plasma membrane
key_finding: Published organelle-specific TMD properties motivated the test; in my hands the effect is too small to place a single protein
context: Comparison of TMDs across the secretory pathway
confidence_and_limitations: High for the population-level claim; does not transfer to individual assignment at the observed effect size.

claim_tested: Hydrophobic matching places AIG1 at the ER
key_finding: ER-only median mean-TM KD 1.542 (n=149) vs PM-only 1.664 (n=1396), Mann-Whitney p=2.74e-10, rank-biserial r=-0.314, heavy overlap. KDE likelihood ratio ER:PM = 1.74 for AIG1 (KD +1.388) and 1.15 for ADTRP (KD +1.484). TM length discarded: 52% of ER-only and 41% of PM-only have mean TM length exactly 21.00 aa with identical medians, so the length difference is an annotation artifact
context: UniProt reviewed human proteome with GO CC annotations
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Negative result that narrows the evidence: the ER case for AIG1 gains essentially nothing from bilayer-thickness matching and rests on the KxKxx motif plus the architectural comparator set.

claim_tested: Independent experimental localisation evidence exists for AIG1
key_finding: AIG1 has 10 rows, all from one weak HPA antibody (confidence 1.532), calling Cytoplasm, Golgi apparatus and Endomembrane system. ADTRP has zero rows. Neither gene appears in any organelle-proteomics dataset (hyperLOPIT, Dynamic Organellar Maps, LOPIT-DC). OpenCell has no tagged line for either
context: 92,113-row human experiments channel; OpenCell line catalogue
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high for absence of evidence. The Golgi/endomembrane call is single-antibody and weak, but it is compatible with an early-secretory protein and incompatible with the mitochondrial call in the HPA record.

claim_tested: AIG1's plasma-membrane GO term has direct-assay support
key_finding: ADTRP carries IDA annotations for GO:0005886, GO:0005901 caveola, GO:0009986 cell surface, GO:0045121 and GO:0044853. AIG1 carries IDA only for GO:0016020 membrane; its GO:0005886 row is EXP with no IDA
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high. Independent database-level confirmation that no curator has recorded a direct assay placing AIG1 at the plasma membrane. QuickGO REST timed out from the executor, so per-annotation reference IDs were not retrieved directly.

claim_tested: AIG1 is an ER-membrane protein rather than a plasma-membrane protein
key_finding: Protease-protection topology mapping was performed on AIG1 IN THE ER MEMBRANE, giving five TM domains with a luminal N-terminus, a cytosolic C-terminus and a hydrophobic stretch between TMD3 and TMD4 that does not cross. AIG1 over-expression raised ER Ca2+ in two cell lines and slightly increased oxidative-stress susceptibility. Highest expression in mouse liver, lung and heart; several tissue-dependent splice variants
context: Mouse tissues (immunoblot) and two over-expressing cell lines
confidence_and_limitations: HIGH importance, moderate confidence. The only AIG1-specific localisation study; NOT cited in UniProt Q9NVV5. Over-expression based; abstract does not name an ER colocalisation marker, so the full text must be read before assigning ECO:0000314. Its 5-TM luminal-N topology conflicts with the AlphaFold 6-TM cytosolic-N model.

citation: This work (AlphaFold AF-Q9NVV5-F1 v6, AF-Q96IZ2-F1 v6)
claim_tested: A hydrophobic stretch between TMD3 and TMD4 does not cross the membrane (PMID:27040980)
key_finding: Every annotated helix starts and ends on opposite sides of the mid-plane with a 25-31 A span: AIG1 TM1 -7.2 to +20.1, TM2 +3.2 to -27.3, TM3 -12.9 to +12.2, TM4 +13.1 to -12.7, TM5 -11.5 to +19.3, TM6 +17.1 to -13.5, per-helix pLDDT 93.7-98.2. ADTRP identical (spans +21.6 to -30.4, pLDDT 96.0-98.4). No re-entrant segment in either model
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high for the geometry, but this is prediction against experiment. AlphaFold has no translocon model and pLDDT at AIG1 residue 1 is 36, so it is weakest exactly where the two topologies disagree. Report as unresolved; both models agree the C-terminus is cytosolic.

claim_tested: An Endo H / glycosylation assay can resolve AIG1 topology and compartment
key_finding: Zero N-X-S/T sequons (X != P) in the full 238-residue AIG1 sequence. No loop and no terminus can carry an N-linked glycan
confidence_and_limitations: High for the scan. Removes the Endo H discriminating test on native protein and explains why PMID:27040980 used protease protection. Weak evidence against a cell-surface pool, since multipass PM proteins usually carry an extracellular glycan, but unglycosylated PM proteins exist.

claim_tested: AIG1 engages COPI coatomer via its C-terminal dilysine
key_finding: Only two physical partners returned: RCHY1 (0.589) and HNRNPL (0.457). No COPA, COPB1, COPB2, COPG1, COPZ1 or ARCN1
confidence_and_limitations: Low. Uninformative rather than negative: COPI binding to a dilysine tail is transient and does not survive most affinity-purification mass-spectrometry workflows. AIG1 is also poorly covered by interaction screens.
